intro.title: From a real puzzle to a visual robot policy.
intro.description: Twelve pieces, two arms. Reconstruct the scene, compose a feedback-driven policy, and improve it through physical trials.
intro.policyInputs: RGB images, robot joint state, and known geometry.
intro.policyBehavior: The graph chooses the next skill; each skill generates targets from the current observations. Independent physical checks evaluate the execution.

real2sim.title: From demonstration to simulation.
real2sim.description: A human demonstration supplies the puzzle and task. RoboSimStudio provides the reconstructed objects, two YAM arms, and contact simulation.
real2sim.scope: Native episode replay of the image-driven policy in the reconstructed RSS workcell. The source video supplies the puzzle and task; the simulation uses an accessible loose-piece layout and keeps the case on the table.

refinement.title: Cyan: find a reachable handover.
refinement.problem: The receiving hand needed a reachable approach and a correctly centered closing contact.
refinement.result: In the continuous twelve-piece run, Cyan passed all four handover checks and continued through placement.

attempts.label: Approach
attempts.diagnosis: The paths ran out of joint reserve or missed the pose.
attempts.change: Move the held piece to a shared workspace, relative to the observed board.
attempts.outcome: Public-geometry rehearsal found screened donor and receiver routes.

attempts.label: Close
attempts.attempt: The new approach reached the piece, but closing was refused.
attempts.diagnosis: The selected finger would penetrate too far.
attempts.change: Reobserve the held piece and recenter the receiving jaw before closing.
attempts.outcome: The next rehearsal passed approach, dual hold, donor withdrawal, and receiver hold.

attempts.label: Verify
attempts.attempt: Repeat the complete transfer in the joined sequence.
attempts.outcome: The continuous twelve-piece run passed all four transfer windows, with an independently verified fresh receiver RGB binding.

evidence.label: See the refinement record
evidence.scope: Recorded attempts, local changes, and verification.

refinement.title: Cyan: continue from the state actually reached.
refinement.problem: A safe intermediate carry stopped just short of its requested waypoint.
refinement.result: The revised skill recovered, replanned, and completed Purple → Cyan → Mint with all 22 checkpoints passing.

attempts.label: Rigid waypoint
attempts.attempt: The first joined rehearsal aborted during carry.
attempts.diagnosis: The hand was stable, but its intermediate position missed the requested tolerance.
attempts.change: Inspect the actual state rather than treating a missed waypoint as a completed motion.
attempts.outcome: The failure record isolated a stable intermediate pose, not a dropped piece.

attempts.label: Local recovery
attempts.attempt: Retain the real intermediate state and check it again.
attempts.diagnosis: A task-independent waypoint can be replaced only after stability and geometry checks.
attempts.change: Verify the held state, acquire fresh RGB, and replan the next leg.
attempts.outcome: The recovery ran in simulation; all three pieces were released and independently verified.

evidence.label: See the refinement record
evidence.scope: Recorded attempts, local changes, and verification.

refinement.title: Cyan: make the release visible.
refinement.problem: The piece was released, but a finger still covered the bead needed by the next visual check.
refinement.result: The wider opening exposed Cyan, earned two accepted observations, and enabled the continuous run to place all twelve pieces.

media.alt: Top-camera crops from two executions: the 55 mm opening covers Cyan's middle bead, while the 75 mm opening reveals it.
media.caption: Actual saved RGB from V10 and V13. Two executions; the public-geometry sweep supplied the opening choice.

evidence.label: See the refinement record
evidence.scope: Recorded attempts, local changes, and verification.

attempts.label: Release
attempts.attempt: The original opening left the next RGB check unaccepted.
attempts.diagnosis: The moving finger still crossed the middle bead in the top image.
attempts.change: Use the recorded joint state and public finger mesh to locate the occlusion.
attempts.outcome: The geometry identified the finger responsible.

attempts.label: Calculate
attempts.diagnosis: A small increase still left some bead rays blocked.
attempts.change: Select the smallest tested opening that cleared every sampled ray and passed the existing guards.
attempts.outcome: The calculation selected a 75 mm opening.

attempts.label: Replay
attempts.attempt: Execute the revised opening and look again.
attempts.outcome: Cyan passed release and next-piece handoff checks; independent audit confirmed all twelve physical placements at the end of the run.

refinement.title: Red: repair the receiving contact.
refinement.problem: A jaw could look loaded while holding the edge of a bead, allowing the piece to roll.
refinement.result: In the continuous twelve-piece run, Red passed both handoffs and its final release. Independent audit confirmed the completed physical assembly.

evidence.label: See the refinement record
evidence.scope: Recorded attempts, local changes, and verification.

attempts.label: Diagnose
attempts.attempt: Earlier handoffs passed, but the held piece rolled during the follow-up motion.
attempts.diagnosis: RGB and robot kinematics placed the bead beyond the front of the blade.
attempts.change: Check the actual finite contact face throughout closing.
attempts.outcome: Saved observations explained why a loaded jaw alone was insufficient.

attempts.label: Repair
attempts.attempt: Keep the donor holding while the receiver is corrected.
attempts.diagnosis: Closing can move the far bead away from its preclose position.
attempts.change: Reopen locally, reobserve, recenter, and reclose under the same geometry checks.
attempts.outcome: The bounded recovery and contact checks passed independent API review.

attempts.label: Rejoin
attempts.attempt: Run both handoffs with fresh receiver bindings in the complete sequence.
attempts.outcome: All eight Red transfer windows and its release passed. The final physical assembly and arms-home state passed independent audit.

refinement.title: Board: recover the rim from another view.
refinement.problem: The arms and puzzle pieces could hide the rim used to estimate the board pose.
refinement.result: The executing graph recovered the board from front and side images while the top-view fit rejected it.

attempts.label: One view
attempts.attempt: The top-camera outline fit lost the rim.
attempts.diagnosis: Hands and pieces interrupted the visible boundary.
attempts.change: Fit the known board outline independently in front and rear images.
attempts.outcome: Recorded-packet checks recovered a top-view failure.

attempts.label: Fixed pair
attempts.attempt: The rear view became blocked during the transfer.
attempts.diagnosis: A fixed camera pair could still lose a required boundary.
attempts.change: Use any two independently supported current views, with the original acceptance checks.
attempts.outcome: Four previously rejected recorded packets were recovered.

attempts.label: Online use
attempts.attempt: Bind the multi-view result to the current observation.
attempts.outcome: The joined V13 execution recovered the rim from front + side views with close cross-view agreement.

media.alt: The same recorded observation from top, front, and side cameras. The top board fit rejects; front and side support a consistent board pose.
media.caption: One actual observation. Two supported views recover the board while the top fit rejects it.

generalization.title: Move the source or the board.
generalization.claim: The same frozen Azure module completed three selected physical rehearsals.
generalization.observed: Nominal; source shifted 3 mm and rotated 3°; board shifted 2 mm and rotated 0.5°. All three released stably, with 0.45–0.75 mm final bead error. The observed source changed the grasp target; the observed board changed the transport target.
generalization.scope: One-piece control · three selected scene variations.

evidence.label: Physical variation results
evidence.scope: Azure only; these are not complete-assembly robustness trials.

generalization.title: Change the input, change the plan.
generalization.claim: The current Cyan and Red functions generate targets from measured poses and robot state.
generalization.observed: A [3, −2, 1] mm board shift moves Cyan's target by the same amount. A 4° source rotation changes Red's first grasp-check orientation by 4°. Increasing board uncertainty can turn an admitted clearance into a refusal. All 16 offline input-response checks passed.
generalization.scope: Offline checks of the actual policy functions.

evidence.label: Inputs and generated outputs
evidence.scope: Demonstrates input-dependent planning and refusal, not physical success under these perturbations.

generalization.title: Recognize shape across appearance.
generalization.claim: Piece identity can be recovered when the colors are shuffled or removed.
generalization.observed: Across three development scenes per appearance, the shape estimator recovered 36/36 pieces with shuffled colors and 36/36 with all-gray pieces. Maximum bead error was 0.75 mm and 0.90 mm respectively.
generalization.scope: Shape perception · three scenes per appearance.

media.alt: A simulated loose-piece scene in which all puzzle pieces share the same gray appearance.
media.caption: All-gray appearance. Identity comes from the known piece shapes.

evidence.label: Appearance recognition results
evidence.scope: Pose and identity estimation; no manipulation success claim.

evidence.label: Shuffled-color scene
evidence.scope: One of the three tested appearance scenes.

cyan-opening.title: Cyan opening: public-geometry diagnosis and actual V13 outcome
cyan-opening.problem: V10 released Cyan, but a 55 mm opening left the middle bead occluded and unaccepted by the next RGB observation.
cyan-opening.selection: Public robot mesh ray prediction found 65 mm cleared 11/13 sampled middle-bead rays, while 75/80/90 mm cleared 13/13. The original six collision groups, board uncertainty and joint limits passed for all tested widths. 75 mm was the smallest fully clear tested option.

image.comparison: Two actual runs, not identical-state A/B trials.

cyan-opening.scope: Actual Cyan visibility repair, release and next-piece handoff within the current continuous all-twelve run. All twelve physical placements and the final physical predicate pass independent review; graph acceptance remains false at 82/84 checkpoints because terminal visual-record admission refuses.

method-alignment.title: RSS / GaP method and actual implementation

summary.title: Reconstruct with RSS
summary.description: Build the scene, task specification, robot embodiment, and contact simulation from the real demonstration.

summary.title: Author with GaP
summary.description: Use the supported graph builder, typed skill contracts, conditional exits, and checkpoint sidecars, guided by the upstream skill and authoring prompts.

summary.title: Control from observation
summary.description: Generate actions from RGB estimates, measured robot joints, public forward kinematics, and known geometry.

summary.title: Rehearse and repair
summary.description: Explore modules and short sequences in parallel, diagnose the failed condition, refine the responsible skill, and reconnect the graph.

summary.title: Evaluate independently
summary.description: Independent physical checkpoints check the actual grasp, handover, placement, stability, and final robot state.

upstream_authoring_basis.actual_authoring_route: The official supported interactive gap.builder route; the upstream skill, paper, prompts and runtime contracts were read and compared. No claim that every headless generation prompt was literally dispatched.
upstream_authoring_basis.runtime_equivalence: Official runtime documentation treats generate, builder and valid JSON as equivalent authoring routes to the same executor.

actual_controller_inputs: Measured robot joint state and public FK
Known public robot, board and piece CAD, task geometry and calibration
Explicitly owned and bounded historical/attachment belief when a target is occluded
method-alignment.modular_refinement: Independent module and short-chain rehearsals produce physical-failure feedback. Local changes are checked and the repaired skills are rejoined; dependent physical stages remain ordered within one shared scene.
method-alignment.independent_evaluation: Simulator ground-truth poses and contacts are permitted in independent hard checkpoints, recorded-state diagnosis and final evaluation. The reviewed production planner obtains scene poses from observation/explicit bounded belief; evaluator state is kept outside policy inputs.

current_execution_measurement.evaluation_basis: Independent audit of saved native poses, velocities, contacts and public goals; no render inference.
current_execution_measurement.terminal_explanation: All twelve physical placements and the original final physical predicate pass. The graph stops in the final Red visual verification because earlier visual receipts were marked unknown_or_conflicted. Red final handoff and finish were not completed; 82/84 checkpoints passed, so graph acceptance remains false.

methodAlignment.title: One graph, locally refined skills.
methodAlignment.description: GaP decomposes the task into reusable skills with typed inputs and independent checkpoints. Failed rehearsals identify the module to repair; the revised skills are then tested together.
